sun.upright:
Mars rules Aries, so when the Nine of Swords turns up in your light it's your own planet keeping you awake. That's worth saying first, because an Aries Sun doesn't usually think of itself as a worrier. You're here to go first, to decide and act and sort out the fallout later. This card is Mars in Gemini, which is Mars stuck up in the head with no obvious door out, and that's the place an Aries Sun finds hardest to be.

From the inside, the energy you'd normally spend doing something turns into thinking about it. You replay what you said in the meeting. You rehearse the argument you're going to have, win it, and then rehearse it again with a better ending. Gemini sits a sextile from Aries, two signs along, a friendly angle, and your fire takes the card's air as fuel, so one thought catches and spreads through you very quickly. That's the trouble at 2 a.m. It's also the way out, because the same speed means that once you actually act on the worry, it tends to burn off fast.

At work it's usually something you started and aren't sure you can finish, or an email you sent in a hurry. With a friend or a sibling it can be guilt about snapping, a small thing that's grown a little every night since. Your body shows it as well, waking tense and wired, ready for a fight with nobody in the room. Whatever it is, do the first concrete bit of it before ten in the morning, the call or the apology or the opening line of the proposal, and see how much of the night's noise is left.
sun.reversed:
You won't call it worry. An Aries Sun meeting this card upside down tends to turn fear into something it's more comfortable with, and that's usually irritation. You're short with people, you pick a fight about the dishwasher, you go for a punishing run at eleven at night. Mars is your ruler, and when its Gemini side is blocked the restlessness still has to go somewhere. It goes outward, at whoever happens to be closest.

The other version is pushing on with no sleep for weeks, because stopping would mean admitting something's wrong. It shows at home first, usually with a partner who's copping the edge of it and has no idea why. At work it looks like taking on more. Next time you feel a row coming, say the sentence underneath it instead, 'I'm worried about the money' or 'I think I stuffed that up', and leave it there.

moon.upright:
Picture the figure in the card, sitting bolt upright with their face in their hands. An Aries Moon wakes like that, all at once, heart going, as though an alarm went off. You don't drift into worry. Your feelings come fast and hot and you usually get to act on them, have it out, go for a walk, be over it by lunch. At four in the morning there's nothing to act on, and that's what makes this card so uncomfortable as your tides.

Mars rules your Moon's sign, so the planet behind the card is the one that runs your emotional life anyway. In Gemini it has no special standing and borrows Mercury's habits, which means it fights with words. The anger that would normally come out and be done with turns into sentences instead, what you should have said, what they said, round and round. Fire and air get on well, and here that means the thoughts fan the feeling and the feeling feeds the thoughts. You may notice it's mostly anger, some of it at yourself for being rattled in the first place.

Sleep is the obvious place, and so is the body, a tight chest, a clenched jaw when you wake. With a partner or a parent it's often one exchange that got under your skin. You'll feel better for moving, so when you wake like that, get up and do ten minutes of something physical in the kitchen, push-ups against the bench, stretches, anything, and only then lie back down.
moon.reversed:
An Aries Moon doesn't like being frightened, so with the card upside down it simply refuses to be. You tell yourself you're fine. You keep busy, and you fall into bed so tired there's no gap for anything to get in. It works for a while. Then it comes out as a flash of temper over nothing, or tears in the car that take you completely by surprise.

Look for it in how you sleep, the nights you crash hard and still wake at three. Look for it with the people you're closest to, because that's where the edge lands first. Mars runs your Moon, and a Mars that's been told to sit still doesn't go quiet, it goes sideways. Once a day, somewhere calm, ask yourself what you're actually scared of and say the answer in one sentence, even if the only person listening is you.

rising.upright:
With Aries rising, Mars is your chart ruler, and this is a Mars card, which makes it more personal for you than for most people. Your rising sign starts things with a bang. You go in fast and head first, and strangers read you as bold and a bit impatient. When the Nine turns up as your mask, the start stalls. You're second-guessing the first move, and that's a state Aries rising doesn't wear well at all.

Mars in Gemini gives your instincts a wordier, sharper edge. You're quick with a comeback and quicker to regret it. Fire catches easily on air, so a small worry shows on your face faster than you'd like, and people meeting you may pick up that you're tense even when you think it's hidden. There's an older link as well. Mars rules the first ten degrees of Aries through the Two of Wands, the card of someone on a castle wall holding a small globe and working out where to go next. That's the healthy version of this energy for you, planning. The Nine is the same planet doing its planning in bed with the light off.

In a new job it's the first fortnight, when you come across keen and a little on edge. On a date it can be the message sent too fast and then reread twelve times. Your face shows tiredness quickly and people tend to read it as crossness. When you catch yourself hesitating at a start, take the smallest version of the first step, one line, one phone call, and let the rest follow.
rising.reversed:
The mask gets harder. Aries rising with the Nine upside down tends to cover worry with bravado, so strangers see someone confident and a bit combative and never guess you were up half the night. A Mars chart ruler that can't move either charges or freezes. So sometimes it's the freeze. The quick start just doesn't happen. The application sits half done, the reply stays unsent, and you hover outside the room.

Interviews and first meetings are where it bites, since you can come across sharper than you mean. Online it's the reply you fire off and then delete. People close to you notice you've gone clipped and short with them. Pick one situation you've been holding back from, and go in plainly, telling the people there a little of what's actually on your mind.

sun.upright:
Mars is in detriment in Taurus, which means the planet behind this card has to work against the grain in your sign, and the effort shows. That's a useful place to start with a Taurus Sun, because worry isn't usually your style. You're here to build something that lasts, money in the bank, a home, a skill you've put years into, and you trust what you can touch. This card is pure thought, all air, and it's landed in the part of you that normally trusts the ground.

The card's element and yours pull in opposite directions, idea against proof. The worry arrives as a thought, what if the job goes, what if the roof needs doing, what if I've got it all wrong, and your sign's instinct is to dig in and hold still until it passes. It doesn't pass quickly. Taurus is fixed and holds on to whatever it's given, worries included. Mars in Taurus is slow and stubborn, and once it's angry it stays angry, so a lot of the night can go on being quietly furious with yourself about something from months ago.

Money is the usual place, the mortgage, the savings account you check twice, the big purchase you're regretting. At work it shows as dread about change, a restructure, a new manager. The body holds it in stiff shoulders and in sleep that comes easily and then stops dead at three. Sit down in daylight with the actual numbers or the actual letter, on paper, with a cup of tea, and look at what's really there.
sun.reversed:
The worry goes underground and sets there. A Taurus Sun turned against this card won't discuss it. You'll just be a bit slower, a bit heavier, and more stubborn about small things, because the big thing is off limits. Mars in detriment in your sign has no easy way to let off steam, so the pressure builds quietly, sometimes for months.

The money side is where to look first, the bill left unopened, the account you've stopped checking. It can also show as holding on too tightly, refusing a change at work you secretly know would be fine. Your partner may be getting a stone wall where there used to be a conversation. Open the envelope, whatever the envelope is for you, with someone sitting beside you who won't make a fuss.

moon.upright:
Look at the bed in this card. It's heavy and carved and quilted, the kind of bed a Taurus Moon would choose, and the person in it can't sleep. That's the hard part of this pairing. Your Moon finds its comfort in the body and in routine, the same pillow, a proper dinner, eight hours, and the Nine arrives in exactly that safe place and keeps you awake inside it.

Taurus sits opposite Scorpio, one of Mars's home signs, which puts Mars in detriment in your Moon's sign, so agitation has no natural route through you. It doesn't come out as a row. It settles in the stomach and the jaw. The elements are at odds too, a mind that won't stop and a body that's tired and wants to be left alone, so you can lie there feeling physically heavy and mentally wired at once, which is an odd combination and a draining one. Gemini and Taurus sit side by side in the zodiac, neighbours with little in common, and that's how it feels, two parts of you that don't speak the same language.

Sleep, obviously, and food, since a Taurus Moon often eats its worry, or stops eating altogether. With a partner you might go quiet and be hard to reach. If it's work on your mind, it's usually about security, whether the job's safe, whether the money will hold. Give your body something to hold on to at bedtime, the same warm drink, clean sheets, your feet flat on the cool floor for a minute if you wake, and let the thoughts run without arguing back.
moon.reversed:
A Taurus Moon with the Nine upside down tends to comfort its way past the worry. Another biscuit, another episode, an afternoon nap, anything that keeps the thought from landing. It's a sensible instinct in small doses. When the worry is real, though, it just gets pushed down into the body, and you end up tired all the time without knowing why.

Sleep can be long and still leave you flat. Money goes on small comforts, and there's a quiet stubbornness with the people around you. Mars in detriment here can't push, so it digs in instead. Your sign's instinct is to wait things out, and some things won't wait. Try naming the worry to one person over a meal, somewhere ordinary, and let the food be a comfort without it having to do all the work.

rising.upright:
People meet a Taurus rising and relax. You come across steady, unhurried, a bit unflappable, and with Venus as your chart ruler you have a pleasant, easy presence. So this card as your mask describes something most people won't see. The calm front is still there. Behind it, Mars in Gemini is going flat out.

In Taurus, Mars is in its detriment, and that means the pushing, aggressive side of you has a very hard time getting out through the front door. What happens instead is that it stays in the face and shoulders. You look calm and your jaw is clenched. Earth and air disagree as well, so the more you think the stiller you get, and people may read that stillness as you being fine, or now and then as you being stubborn. Neither is quite right. You're hesitating because you can't see the ground under the next step, and your whole sign is built on checking the ground.

At work you're probably the one everyone assumes has it handled, which means nobody asks. A friend may mention you've seemed quiet. In a new situation, a meeting, a first date, you'll hang back longer than you usually would. If someone asks how you are, give them one true detail about your week, even a small one, and see what they do with it.
rising.reversed:
The calm face turns into a wall. Taurus rising can go very still under pressure, and with this card reversed you may be so composed that people stop checking on you at all. The worry doesn't show, and so nobody offers to help. Or the stillness tips into stubbornness, digging in over small decisions because the big one feels out of your hands.

At work that means refusing to hand anything over, and with friends it's plans cancelled with a vague excuse. The neck and shoulders carry it, and you may notice you're grinding your teeth. Your chart ruler is Venus, and Venus likes things to look pleasant, which makes the front very convincing. Let one person see you rattled, briefly, and ask them for something specific, a lift, an hour, an opinion.

sun.upright:
This is one of Gemini's own cards. The Nine of Swords covers the middle ten degrees of your sign, the second decan, which Mars rules, so when it turns up in your light it isn't a visitor from somewhere else. It's a part of Gemini, the part that argues. Your Sun wants to know things, talk, connect ideas and keep moving between them, and this card is that same gift aimed back at you after dark.

Mars has no dignity in Gemini. It's neither strong nor weak there, just a guest who picks up Mercury's habits, so it fights with questions and sentences. Same element on both sides turns everything up, the good and the too much. You can see six sides of every problem, which is brilliant in a meeting and exhausting at 2 a.m. when all six are arguing. The Lovers is Gemini's Major, and choosing runs all through your sign. This card is often a choice you keep reopening, decided at midnight, undecided by breakfast.

At work it's usually a decision, two job offers, whether to speak up, which version of the plan to back. With a brother or sister, or whoever you talk to most, it can be a conversation you keep rewriting in your head. Your phone is involved, it nearly always is with this pairing. Pick one of the options, write down why in three lines, and tell one person which one you chose.
sun.reversed:
For a Gemini Sun the reversed Nine often looks like never being alone with your own thoughts. A podcast on in the shower, the phone in bed, three conversations going at once, so the worry never gets a quiet moment to speak. It feels like being busy and sociable. Underneath, it's a way of keeping one particular thought off the table.

Or the chatter turns into cleverness at your own expense, jokes about how badly you're doing that nobody quite laughs at. You'll see it with friends who've heard the funny version and never the real one, and in sleep that only comes once you're completely worn out. Because this card is native to your sign, the noise feels normal, and that's what makes it easy to miss. Give the thought a proper slot, fifteen minutes with a pen and no screen, and see what it actually says.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon settles by talking. You feel better once you've put a thing into words and said it to someone, ideally two or three someones, and heard what they think. This card is the version of that where there's nobody to talk to. The house is quiet, everyone's asleep, and the conversation carries on anyway, with you playing both parts.

The Nine belongs to your Moon's sign. It's the second decan of Gemini, Mars in a Mercury sign, so it speaks your emotional language fluently, and air on air amplifies it. The mind that normally soothes you by naming things starts naming everything that could go wrong. It's fast and it's persuasive. Mars adds heat, so the voice isn't only anxious, it's a bit nasty as well, picking at what you said and the way you said it.

Late-night scrolling is the classic sign, the news, looking up symptoms, reading back through an old message thread. With a sibling or a close friend there may be a misunderstanding you haven't cleared up. Sleep suffers in a shallow, busy way, with lots of dreams and lots of talking in them. Keep a notebook by the bed and, when it starts, write the conversation down instead of having it, then shut the notebook and turn the lamp off.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Gemini Moon, the chatter can go quiet in a way that isn't restful at all. You stop telling people things. The messages pile up unread, the group chat carries on without you, and from outside it looks like you're just busy. Mostly you're avoiding the conversation where someone asks how you really are. Your Moon processes out loud, and when that outlet closes, the feelings stack up with nowhere to go.

The other side is worry that's turned into background noise, so constant you don't notice it any more, only that you're tired and a bit flat. Friendships go cool, and there's a restless sort of boredom, flicking between things without settling. Send one message to the friend you'd normally tell first, and put something true in it.

rising.upright:
Mercury rules Gemini, so with Gemini rising your chart ruler is Mercury, and this card puts Mars right on top of it. That's what people meet. Normally you come across quick, curious and easy to talk to. With the Nine as your mask you still come across quick, only there's a wire in it, faster talking, a sharper joke, a slight sense that you're somewhere else.

The card is native to your rising sign, the middle decan of Gemini, so no translation is needed. The world gets Mars in Gemini straight, which at its best is a mind that cuts to the point and at its worst is a mind that cuts. Same element, same language, everything louder. You'll catch yourself replying too quickly, filling silences, having an opinion ready before the question's finished. From the inside it feels like nerves. From outside it can pass for confidence, or occasionally for not listening.

Meetings show it, especially the ones where you're new or being assessed. On a first date you may talk a lot and remember very little of it afterwards. Online is the big one, the comment you fire back, the post you wish you hadn't made. Before you reply to anything that stings, wait for one full cup of tea to be made and drunk.
rising.reversed:
When the Nine turns over for Gemini rising, the quick, chatty front can go brittle. You're funny and fast and people like you, and you're also exhausted, and the effort of keeping the patter going shows in odd moments, a blank look mid-sentence, a joke that lands wrong. Some Gemini risings go the other way and simply stop turning up, too tired for the small talk that usually comes free.

You'll know it by the meetings you mentally leave halfway through and the event you cancel at the last minute. Messages are the giveaway, long gaps and then a flood. Mars in Gemini at the front of the chart keeps you sharp, and sharp gets tiring. Choose one setting where you can drop the performance, a person or a place, and go there before you're completely run down.

sun.upright:
Mars is in fall in Cancer. It can't do its job directly here, so it finds an indirect route, and that's the key to this card turning up in a Cancer Sun's light. You're here to look after people and keep a home safe. When something threatens that, you can't just charge at it. So the fight turns inward, and at night it becomes this card.

The worry is almost always about someone else, the kids, a parent getting older, a partner who's been quiet, and underneath it there's guilt. Did I do enough, did I say the wrong thing, should I have noticed sooner. Gemini and Cancer are next-door signs with very different habits, and air and water don't mix without some kind of introduction. So your mind produces a list of things that could go wrong while your feelings sit there unnamed. You know you're upset. It's much harder to say exactly why.

Family is where to look, especially a parent or a child you feel responsible for. At home you might be doing a lot of checking, the doors, the stove, the weather warnings. At work the caring role you play is heavier than usual, and people are leaning. Ask the person you're worried about how they actually are, directly, and believe what they tell you.
sun.reversed:
The worry turns into looking after everyone. A Cancer Sun meeting this card reversed will organise, cook, ring round and fix, and never once mention they haven't slept properly in a fortnight. Mars in fall does its fighting through the back door, and here the back door is busyness. It feels caring, and it is. It's also a way of making sure nobody asks you anything.

Sometimes it comes out as moodiness instead, going into your shell, sulking a bit, feeling hurt that nobody noticed. Home and family carry it, and so does your stomach. The people close to you may feel a tension in the house they can't put a name to. Tell one person in the family, the one who'd cope best, that you're struggling, and let them do one practical thing for you.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon at home, feeling everything at full volume and remembering all of it. This card arriving in your tides tends to bring the past into the bedroom. Often it's an old worry, something from years ago that comes back at 3 a.m. in full colour, as if it happened last week.

Mars is in fall in Cancer, which is where it's weakest. Anger in a Cancer Moon has trouble coming out cleanly, so it curls inward and turns into hurt, or into guilt. You go over what you should have said to your mother, your ex, your oldest friend. Gemini sits right beside Cancer and the two have almost nothing in common. The card thinks in words and your Moon feels in waves, and air and water need to be introduced before they'll cooperate. At night nobody does the introducing. The thoughts churn up the feelings and the feelings give the thoughts more to chew on.

Sleep, food and family are the three places to watch. You might wake at the same time every night, or find yourself eating late for comfort. A parent, or someone who once played that part, may be on your mind a lot. Put a glass of water and a pen beside the bed. If you wake, write down the name of whoever you're thinking about and one thing you'd want them to know, then turn over.
moon.reversed:
The shell closes. A Cancer Moon with the Nine reversed usually stops talking about what's wrong and gets very good at looking okay. Mars in fall can't push its way out, so the feeling goes somewhere quiet and stays there. Old memories get tidied into a box, and the box gets heavier every month.

Or it runs the other way and the past floods in during the day, a song in the supermarket, a smell, and suddenly you're in tears by the frozen peas. Family gatherings find you pleasant and far away, and sleep is heavy and doesn't refresh you. You might be avoiding a phone call to someone you love. Make that call, or a shorter version of it, and let them hear in your voice that you're not quite yourself.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising meets the world through a shell. You come across kind, careful, a little reserved, someone who takes a while to open up and then looks after everybody. The Moon rules your rising sign, so your first reactions follow your mood closely, and people can often read your week in your face before you've said a word.

This card as your mask brings Mars in Gemini to the front door, and Mars falls in Cancer, which is the technical term for its weakest placement, so its defensiveness comes out sideways. You might be shorter with strangers than you mean to be, or more guarded, or both. Gemini and Cancer are neighbouring signs that don't understand each other much, and it shows in how you're coming across. There's quick, nervous talk on the surface and a lot of feeling held very still underneath. People may pick up the tiredness first.

At work, new colleagues could read you as cool or distracted when you're actually worried about home. With neighbours or at the school gate you'll keep it brief. In a new relationship you might test the other person a little, asking the same question two different ways. When someone asks if you're alright, try saying 'not really, but I'll be okay', and notice who stays for the rest of the conversation.
rising.reversed:
The shell can go fully shut. Cancer rising under the reversed Nine might stop turning up to things, say yes and then cancel, or keep every conversation so light that nobody gets close enough to notice. You still look pleasant. You're just not really there, and people who don't know you well may decide you're aloof.

Mars in fall at the front of the chart can also make you prickly, snapping at a stranger and then feeling awful about it for a week. Work, neighbours and family settings all get this version, especially where you've gone into host mode to keep the questions away. Say yes to one small invitation and stay for an hour, with no escape plan and no excuse ready.

sun.upright:
Leo is the Sun's own sign, and a Leo Sun is here to be seen doing something that matters, generously and with some flair. This card in your light usually brings a very Leo fear, the fear of being embarrassed. Did it look stupid. Did they laugh. Was the thing you made any good. It's a proud sign's version of 3 a.m., and pride makes it harder to tell anyone.

In Leo, Mars has no special dignity and takes on the Sun's colouring, so it's a fire that wants recognition. In Gemini, though, it's all in the head. Gemini and Leo are two signs apart, a sextile, which is a friendly angle, and your fire takes to the card's air quickly, so the worry spreads fast and gets dramatic. One lukewarm comment becomes a verdict on your whole career. Mars also rules the last ten degrees of Leo through the Seven of Wands, the card of holding your ground from below with everyone coming at you, so your sign knows how to defend itself. At night it defends against critics who aren't in the room.

A creative project is the obvious place, something you've made or put out and are waiting to hear about. At work it's a presentation, a review, a promotion. In love it can be the fear that you're adored a little less than you used to be. Show the unfinished thing to one person who's on your side, and ask them what they liked about it.
sun.reversed:
Pride shuts the door. A Leo Sun with this card turned over usually won't admit to being worried at all, and the effort of looking magnificent while privately rattled can be enormous. You keep performing, big energy, big laugh, and you're running on almost nothing underneath.

The other version is hiding. You don't put the work out, you don't go for the role, because being seen to fail feels worse than never trying. Creative projects stall at ninety percent, and a partner gets the bright public face and none of the truth. The Sun rules your sign, and a Sun behind cloud still wants to be warm, so the frustration builds. Tell one person the specific thing you're afraid they'll think of you, word for word.

moon.upright:
Nine swords on a black wall and one person in bed with their face covered. For a Leo Moon, the covered face is the part to notice. You need warmth, loyalty and the sense that you matter to the people you love, and when that feels uncertain you'd sooner hide than ask. As your tides, this card is often that exact fear, lying awake wondering whether you're loved as much as you love.

Gemini and Leo are a friendly sextile apart, and air stirs up fire, so the thought catches quickly and burns hot. A small thing, a partner who seemed distracted, a friend who didn't reply, becomes a whole story by two in the morning. Leo is fixed, so once the story is written it's hard to rewrite. The Sun rules Leo and colours Mars there, so this is a Mars that takes things personally. You aren't only worried, you're hurt and a bit indignant, and then embarrassed about being indignant.

With a partner it's the need for reassurance you don't want to ask for. With children or friends it can be feeling taken for granted. Sleep comes in bursts, and mornings can be heavy. Ask for the reassurance plainly, in daylight, without dressing it up as a joke, something like 'I've been feeling a bit left out, can we do something together this weekend?'
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon doesn't sulk quietly, and when the Nine turns over the hurt usually comes out as drama or as frost. You might make a scene over something small because the big thing, feeling unappreciated, is too exposing to say. Or you go regal and cold and wait for somebody to notice. Underneath both is the same worry, that you matter less to them than they do to you.

A partner and close friends feel it most, and sometimes kids, where you're giving a lot and privately keeping score. Sleep tends to be fine until something wakes you, and then it's gone for the night. Your Moon needs to feel generous again, so do something warm for someone with nobody watching, and see how it settles you.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks in and the room warms up. You come across bright, confident, well put together, and the Sun, your chart ruler, gives you a presence people remember. With the Nine of Swords in the mask position, the show is still on and the performer is tired.

Mars borrows the Sun's colours in Leo and wants to look strong, and in Gemini it's restless and wordy. With the card's air feeding your rising sign's fire, there's plenty of energy on the surface, quick talk, big gestures, but it's nervous energy, and people who know you can tell. Strangers mostly won't. Mars rules the last decan of Leo through the Seven of Wands, a figure on a hill fending off six staves, and that's roughly how first meetings may feel, as if you're defending yourself against a criticism nobody has made. You might oversell, or get prickly at a mild question.

At work it's the pitch or the performance review. Socially it's the party where you're the life of it and home by ten, wrung out. Your appearance often shows it first, and you'll either make a huge effort or stop bothering. Go into the next big room having told one person there how you're really doing, so at least someone knows.
rising.reversed:
The mask cracks, or it gets stuck on. Leo rising with the Nine reversed can overdo the brightness until it looks forced, laughing too loudly, dressing up to hide how tired you are. Or you pull back from being seen at all, skip the event, turn the camera off in the meeting, and then feel ashamed of hiding. With the Sun as your chart ruler you're used to being the warm one in the room, so being dim for a while feels like failing.

Online is where the gap between what you're posting and how you're sleeping gets widest. Friends may say you seem different. Choose one place where you're allowed to be off, a friend's kitchen, a long walk on your own, and give yourself an evening there with nothing to perform.

sun.upright:
Mercury rules Gemini and it rules Virgo, so the card's sign and yours share a landlord, and they still don't get on. Gemini and Virgo square each other, both mutable, and the friction between them forces something to change. A Virgo Sun is here to be useful, to get things right, to notice what needs fixing. With the Nine of Swords in your light, all that noticing turns into a list of everything that's wrong, and most of the list is about you.

Mars has no rank of its own in Virgo and takes on Mercury's habits, so it works through detail. That's the voice at 3 a.m. going through the spreadsheet, the email, the thing you said at the barbecue, line by line. Earth and air don't trust each other, idea against proof. You want evidence and the card hands you speculation, so you try to fix it with more checking, which only feeds it. Virgo also feels guilty very easily. The error might be tiny and you'll still have it on a loop.

At work it's the mistake in the report, or the fear there's one you haven't found yet. With your health routines it can be over-checking, the new diet, the step count, the fitness tracker at midnight. At home it's the jobs not done. Write the list out in full, cross out everything you can't do anything about by Friday, and do one thing from what's left.
sun.reversed:
When the Nine turns over for a Virgo Sun, the worry tends to go into overwork. You don't lie awake, exactly. You get up at five and start on the inbox, and it feels productive. The anxiety has found a job and it's very good at it. What doesn't get done is anything restful, because rest feels like slacking, and Virgo can call this being conscientious for a long time before admitting it's scared.

The body usually registers it first, tension, a fussy stomach, a cold that hangs around, and then work, where you're doing the job of two people and quietly resenting it. Mars in a Mercury sign works overtime when it's blocked. Book one hour in the week that's for nothing useful at all, and keep it even when something urgent comes up.

moon.upright:
Order is what calms a Virgo Moon. A tidy bench, a routine, the sense that you've done what you could. The Nine arrives in your tides as the opposite, a mind picking at loose ends in the dark, and because you feel safest when things are handled, the unhandled ones feel dangerous at night.

Gemini squares Virgo, and the card's airy, jumping thoughts grind against a Moon that wants things sorted and put away. It's idea against matter again. You'll recognise the body getting drawn in, too, the way a small ache at 2 a.m. starts to feel like a sign of something, or a tight chest after a bad day becomes a whole worry of its own. Mars is only a visitor in Virgo and speaks in Mercury's voice there, precise and critical, which is why the nights have that picky, itemised quality. Nothing is too small to go over.

Sleep, clearly, and the body's small signals. At work you may be the person holding everyone's loose ends and feeling responsible for all of them. If you care for a parent or a friend who's struggling, that's likely where the worry lives. Give the worrying a fixed appointment, half an hour at six in the evening with a notebook, and when it turns up at night, tell it to wait for six.
moon.reversed:
A Virgo Moon under this card reversed can turn worry into a routine so tight it squeaks. Same breakfast, same checks, same order of doing things, and if anything's out of place the whole day feels wrong. It looks like good habits. Underneath is a fear that something will go wrong the minute you stop. Mars in a Mercury sign gets fussy when it has nowhere else to go.

Criticism is the other giveaway, of yourself mostly and then of a partner or housemates, the dishes stacked wrong, the towel on the floor. Sleep can be long enough and still leave you tired. Let one small thing stay undone on purpose, the drawer, the washing, and watch what the worry does with the gap.

rising.upright:
With Virgo rising, Mercury runs your chart, and people meet you as capable, modest and a bit watchful, the one who's already noticed what's wrong with the room. This card in your mask gives that watchfulness an edge. You arrive prepared, over-prepared really, and slightly braced for something.

Mars in Virgo is a guest with no special standing, and it takes on Mercury's precise, critical tone. Gemini squares Virgo, a friction pairing, and with air and earth at odds your head is racing while your manner stays tidy and polite. Strangers may read it as competence. People who know you will see the small tells, the double-checking, the apology before you've done anything, the way you rehearse what you're going to say. You may feel you're being assessed everywhere you go, which is tiring, and to be honest, most of the assessing is being done by you.

Job interviews and first days are where it's loudest. In email it shows as the message redrafted six times. With new people you may be harder on yourself than usual, and it can leak out as being hard on them. Next time you walk into a room like that, go in with one thing deliberately unprepared, and see how it goes.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the careful front gets very brittle. Virgo rising might apologise for everything, or go the other way and turn sharp, correcting, pointing things out, getting in first before anyone can criticise you. Either way you're braced for a judgement nobody has actually made. Mercury, your chart ruler, tries under pressure to control very tightly what comes out of your mouth.

At work colleagues might find you hard to help. In a new friendship you may hold back so much that it never gets going. Your face shows the tiredness and your posture stiffens. The square from Gemini keeps the mind busy looking for the next thing to fix. Say one imperfect thing in a meeting, a half-formed idea, and let it stand without explaining it.

sun.upright:
Mars is in detriment in Libra, the sign opposite its home, so the planet of conflict has to work against the grain in you. That won't surprise a Libra Sun. You're here to make things fair and keep people together, and you'll go a long way to avoid a row. The Nine of Swords is what happens to the row you avoided. It doesn't disappear. It comes back at night, and you have it with yourself.

Gemini and Libra are a trine apart, both air, so this card speaks your language easily and the shared element makes it louder. That's why it's so articulate. You can argue both sides, you can see how you were unfair and how they were, and you replay the conversation looking for the version where everyone ends up happy. There usually isn't one. Libra's instinct is to keep weighing, and Mars in your sign is weak enough that the decision never quite gets made.

With a partner it's usually the thing you didn't say. At work it's a disagreement with a colleague you smoothed over, or a question of fairness, who gets what, that you're stuck on. Friendships too, especially one where you've been doing all the giving. Say the disagreement once, in daylight, calmly and in one sentence, and then let the other person answer.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun turned upside down by this card will often keep the peace so hard that nobody knows there's a problem, including you on some days. You smile, you agree, you're lovely company, and then you lie awake running the argument you'll never have. You might not even call it anger. It feels like tiredness. Mars in detriment gets resentful when it isn't allowed to speak.

A partner feels it most, and so does the friendship where you're always the one who adjusts. At work it can be a slow burn over something unfair you've never raised. Eventually it leaks out as a cool, polite distance that stings worse than a fight would have. Pick one small thing you've been letting go and raise it, kindly and plainly.

moon.upright:
You feel safe when things are calm between you and the people you love. That's the whole of a Libra Moon's need, more or less, and it's why this card hurts. Drawn for your tides, it often means lying beside someone who's asleep while you go over what went wrong between you, whether it was your fault, whether it can be fixed.

Libra is one of the two signs where Mars is in detriment. Anger is hard for your Moon to feel, let alone show, so it tends to come out as worry, which feels safer and is far more tiring. The card and your Moon share an element and sit a trine apart, so the thinking comes easily and doesn't stop. You're very good at seeing the other person's side. In the small hours that turns into seeing every side and taking responsibility for all of them.

With a partner it's the unresolved thing from the weekend. With a close friend it might be feeling you were unfair, or that they were and you couldn't say so. Your surroundings matter a lot to a Libra Moon, so a messy bedroom or a noisy street makes the nights worse. Before bed, make the room nice, things put away, soft light, and leave the conversation for a morning when you've both had breakfast.
moon.reversed:
When this card is reversed on a Libra Moon, you may insist everything's fine for so long that you start to believe it. The peace holds on the surface. Inside, Mars in detriment is sulking, and it comes out in small ways, a sigh, a sharp word at the dishwasher, a sudden need to be on your own for an hour.

Partners and housemates get the edge of it, in the things that go unsaid, and your sleep turns light and easily broken. You might be at your most charming with strangers and flat at home. Your friends may not notice at all, which is partly the point. Tell your partner or your closest friend one thing that's been bothering you, and don't soften it three times before it comes out.

rising.upright:
Libra rising is the gracious one. Venus rules your rising sign, and people meet you as charming, fair-minded and easy to be around, with a knack for putting others at ease. When this card is your mask, you're still putting everyone at ease. You're just doing it on four hours' sleep.

Mars in detriment in Libra struggles to show any edge on the surface, so whatever's bothering you is tucked well out of sight. Gemini trines Libra, air to air, and people often meet a lot of quick, pleasant talk, which is part of how you cope. Nobody would guess. The tension is that Libra rising reads a room so well that you pick up every tiny sign of disapproval and take it home with you. You leave a meeting feeling fine and wake at three remembering someone's expression.

At work it's the colleague you've been pleasant to while privately furious. On a date you'll be lovely company and then lie awake wondering whether you talked too much. With friends you might say yes to things you don't want to do. Next time someone asks for something you'd sooner not give, say you'll think about it and give your answer the next day.
rising.reversed:
The charm starts to cost you. Libra rising under the reversed Nine can agree to everything, smile through everything, and quietly run out of whatever was fuelling it. Or the pleasant front slips, a flash of irritation escapes with a stranger, and you're mortified by it for days. When you're depleted you tend to reach for looking nice as a kind of armour, which is Venus, your chart ruler, doing her best.

Colleagues see it before friends do. It's in the social plans you dread and in a face that's tired under the make-up or the neat shirt. Mars in detriment won't let you be cross in public, so it builds. Say no to one request, politely and without an excuse, and leave it at that.

sun.upright:
Traditionally Mars rules Scorpio, so this card comes to a Scorpio Sun with the authority of your own sign's ruler. Mars at home in Scorpio is powerful and private, the fighter who waits. In Gemini it's a completely different animal, and Gemini and Scorpio are a quincunx apart, five signs, with nothing in common and constant small adjustments between them. So your own planet has turned up talking fast, doubting, second-guessing, which is a long way from how you like to operate.

From the inside it's often suspicion. What did they mean by that, who knows what, what aren't they telling me. Scorpio needs to get to the bottom of things, and this card gives you a bottomless question to chew on at night. There's grief in it too. Mars rules the first ten degrees of Scorpio through the Five of Cups, the cloaked figure staring at three spilled cups, so your sign knows regret well. The Nine can be regret that has hardened into self-accusation.

In a relationship it's trust, whether you can, whether you should, what they did last year. At work it can be power, who's got it, whether you're about to lose it. Or it's a secret of your own that you're tired of keeping. Say one true sentence to the person it concerns, and then stop talking and let them respond.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun under the reversed Nine goes very quiet and very controlled. The worry gets locked away where nobody can see it, and you carry on with a sort of grim focus. Mars rules your sign, and a cornered Mars doesn't complain. It watches, and waits, and every so often it strikes at the wrong person. The quincunx with Gemini makes it worse, because the chatter in your head doesn't suit how you like to process, slowly and alone.

In a relationship it turns into checking, the phone, the bank statement, the timeline. At work it becomes a grudge. In the body it's tension you've stopped noticing because it's been there so long. Pick one person you actually trust and tell them the thing you've been guarding, all of it, including the part you're ashamed of.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moon feelings run deep, last long, and don't get shown to many people. This card in your tides can bring up something old, a betrayal, a loss, a jealousy, and put it on repeat. Mars rules your Moon's sign, so the planet behind the card already has keys to the house, and it knows exactly where you keep things.

The strain is in the quincunx. Gemini and Scorpio share nothing, and the card's fast, talky, restless mind sits badly with a Moon that processes slowly, privately, all the way down. You want to feel it fully and be done. The card keeps offering you another angle, another theory, another thing they might have meant. Water and air are strangers to each other, and at night they don't get the chance to become anything else. Mars also rules the first decan of Scorpio through the Five of Cups, and the Nine on your Moon can carry that same weight of old regret.

In a relationship it's jealousy, or the fear of being left. With family it can be an old story that still stings. Sleep may be heavy and full of intense dreams. When it comes up, write out exactly what you're afraid of, in full, and then shred the page, which Scorpio tends to find oddly satisfying.
moon.reversed:
The feeling goes underground. A Scorpio Moon meeting this card reversed can lock something away so thoroughly that you stop admitting it's there. Then it drives your behaviour anyway, a coldness towards someone you used to love, a refusal to be vulnerable, sleep that's always slightly on guard. You're good at keeping secrets, including from yourself.

Partners and family feel it, and old grudges run the show. Sometimes it's the opposite and you can't let something go, and going over it eats hours of the day. Mars at home in your Moon's sign is strong either way. Choose one old hurt and talk it through with someone outside the situation, a counsellor or a friend with no stake in it.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising already comes across as intense, watchful and hard to read. Traditionally Mars is your chart ruler, so a Mars card in the mask position sits right on the steering of your chart. People meet you and feel they're being assessed. With the Nine here, you probably are assessing them, and yourself, and the exits.

Mars at home in Scorpio is controlled and patient. In Gemini it's jumpy and wordy, and the two signs are a quincunx apart, awkward and always adjusting. So there's a strange flicker in how you come across, the usual stillness with something restless underneath, a glance at the phone, a sudden edge in your voice. The card's air and your rising sign's water don't naturally meet, and strangers may read you as cool when you're actually on high alert. You might be scanning every room for the person who doesn't like you.

At a new job you may keep your cards close and read everyone before you say much. On a date it's the careful questions and the background research. Online it's looking people up and finding more than you wanted to know. Before the next first meeting, decide on one thing about yourself you'll tell them freely, and tell them early.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising in the grip of the reversed Nine can go into full armour. You give nothing away at all, and people find you intimidating when underneath you're frightened. Or the defences slip in odd ways, a cutting remark, a sudden coldness, a suspicion you say out loud before you've checked it. Scorpio rising is used to seeing through people, and this card turns that sight into suspicion.

New workplaces and new relationships bring it out, anywhere people need to trust you quickly. You might be hard to approach and then wonder why nobody approaches. Your chart ruler, pushed down, tends to leak out as sharpness. Let one small softness show in the next conversation that matters, a laugh at yourself, a question about them.

sun.upright:
Gemini is Sagittarius's opposite sign, so this card sits right across the axis from your Sun. That's the shape of the trouble. You're here for the big picture, freedom, meaning, the next horizon, and Gemini is all detail, all small print. The Nine of Swords brings you the small print at 3 a.m. and none of the view.

Mars is only a guest in Sagittarius and takes on Jupiter's colouring, and Jupiter makes things bigger. So when a Sagittarius Sun worries, it doesn't worry small. It goes straight to the worst case on the widest scale, the whole plan was wrong, the whole belief was foolish. The card's air and your fire egg each other on, which makes it quick and bright and hard to put out. There's a loss of faith in it, and for a sign that runs on optimism, that's very disorienting. The opposition pulls toward balance, and the balance you need is some of Gemini's patience with facts.

Study and travel are common ground for it, the visa, the course, the move overseas you've half committed to. At work it can be a big bet you made. With a belief, spiritual or political, it may be a doubt you didn't see coming. Take the biggest fear and break it into three questions you could actually find answers to, and start with the easiest.
sun.reversed:
Sagittarius Suns meeting this card reversed tend to outrun the worry. You book something, plan something, start a new thing, keep moving so the thought can't catch up. It can look like optimism. Some of it is. Some of it is running. The opposite happens too, when the usual cheer switches off completely, and that frightens the people who rely on it.

Look at the plans that multiply and never land, the money spent on escape, the restlessness that makes it hard to sit through a whole film. Jupiter's colouring on Mars makes the escape bigger. With a partner, the worry might come out as blunt remarks you regret later. Stay put for one whole weekend without a plan, and let the thought catch up with you.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. Space, a horizon, a bit of hope, the feeling that there's somewhere to go if things get tight. This is the least roomy card in the deck, one person in one bed in a black room, and in your tides it tends to feel like being trapped with your own head.

Gemini opposes Sagittarius, so the card's anxious detail pulls against a Moon that normally soothes itself with the long view. Mars in Sagittarius borrows Jupiter's size, so feelings come big. A small worry about money becomes a fear you'll never be free. A tense phone call becomes the end of the friendship. Fire and air are friendly elements, and that's part of the trouble, since the thoughts fan the feeling faster than you can think it through. You might notice you've lost your sense of humour, which is usually the first thing a Sagittarius Moon reaches for.

Sleep goes when you've been indoors too long. With a partner it can be feeling hemmed in, and then guilty for feeling it. Plans and travel may be on hold, which makes it worse. Get outside for a long walk somewhere with a view, a hill or a beach or the high end of the park, and leave the phone at home.
moon.reversed:
The Sagittarius Moon version of hiding is joking. With the Nine turned over you might make everything into a funny story, the break-up, the bad news, the sleepless week, so that nobody, including you, has to take it seriously. Or you leave, a trip, a new flat, a sudden plan, and the worry comes too, packed in with the socks.

Socially you're great company. At home you can't settle, and sleep comes easier away than in your own bed. Mars in your Moon's sign takes on Jupiter's appetite for more, so escape can get expensive, and partners may feel you're never quite there. Tell the story once without the jokes, to someone who'll let the quiet part land, and don't rescue them from it.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in open-faced and cheerful, a bit loud, very honest, ready for whatever's next. Jupiter rules your rising sign and gives you that sense of plenty. This card as your mask takes some of the ease out of the stride. You're still friendly, but there's a tired look behind it, and the jokes are coming a beat too fast.

Mars in Sagittarius has no dignity and is coloured by Jupiter, so it's blunt and a bit over the top. In Gemini it gets quick and wordy, and Gemini sits opposite your rising sign, which puts the card squarely in front of you, like someone standing across the room. Your instinct is to be frank, and this card sharpens frankness until it can cut. You might say what's on your mind a bit too directly and then lie awake over it. With air and fire together, first impressions happen fast, for better and worse.

At work it shows in meetings where you speak first and think after. Socially it can be the comment at dinner that lands wrong. When you travel, and you probably want to, it might be a restlessness that follows you from place to place. Before you say the frank thing, ask one question first, and listen properly to the answer.
rising.reversed:
When the Nine is upside down, Sagittarius rising can turn the cheer up so loud it's a bit much. Big stories, big laughs, big plans announced to people you've just met, and all of it keeps anyone from asking a quiet question. Or it goes the other way, the famous openness closes, and you're oddly short with people who expected your usual warmth.

Parties and new workplaces bring it out, and so does being online, where you may post a lot and say very little. A partner often feels the gap between the public you and the one at home. Jupiter, your chart ruler, overdoes things under strain. Pick one person and let them see the version of you that's worried, without making a joke of it at the end.

sun.upright:
Mars is exalted in Capricorn, an honoured guest in your sign, drive at its most disciplined and effective. That's the good news with this card for a Capricorn Sun. The same planet that keeps you awake is the one that, in your sign, gets things built. Mars also rules the middle ten degrees of Capricorn through the Three of Pentacles, the card of skilled work done properly alongside other people, so your sign already knows what to do with this energy in daylight.

The difficulty is Gemini. The card's sign and yours are a quincunx apart with nothing in common, and air and earth are opposed, talk against proof. Capricorn wants a plan. The Nine gives you forty scenarios in the middle of the night and no plan at all. You're responsible, usually the one holding things together, and the worry is almost always about failing at that. What if the business doesn't make it, what if you've let the family down, what if people find out you're not coping.

At work it's the thing you're accountable for. With money it's the long-term numbers, super, the mortgage, the kids' future. With an ageing parent it can be the responsibilities quietly shifting onto you. Turn the worry into a plan with dates on it, even a rough one, on paper, and show it to one person whose judgement you trust.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with the Nine reversed usually works harder. That's the reflex. Worried about the business, put in more hours. Worried about the family, take on more of the load. Mars exalted in your sign is superb at effort, so the worry gets converted into productivity and nobody, including you, notices what it costs. Capricorn is proud of its self-reliance, and this card upside down uses that pride against you.

The cost turns up eventually, in the back and shoulders, in a short temper at home, in weekends that don't feel like rest. It can also show as rigidity at work, refusing help because asking would mean admitting a problem. Hand one responsibility to someone else and don't check up on how they're doing it.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest when things are under control. You handle feelings the way you'd handle a project, sensibly, privately, and preferably without making a fuss. The Nine of Swords is the hour when that system stops working. At night there's nothing to manage and nobody to be competent for, and the feelings you've been filing away all day come out at once.

The card's air and your Moon's earth are opposed elements, so you get a stream of thoughts that can't be tested until morning, and your Moon hates anything that can't be tested. The quincunx between Gemini and Capricorn makes it more awkward still. Mars being exalted in Capricorn helps, though. It gives your Moon a real capacity for effort under pressure, so once there's something to do, you'll do it well. It's lying there with nothing to do that's hard. Plenty of Capricorn Moons were the responsible child in the family, and this card can bring that old weight back.

Work is the obvious place, a deadline, a mistake, a role you're afraid you're not up to. With a parent, particularly a stern one or one who's started to need you, it may be old duty mixed with new worry. Your body might carry it as a deep tiredness. Book a time in the morning, a proper slot in your diary, to deal with the thing, and when it wakes you, tell yourself it's booked.
moon.reversed:
Capricorn Moons are experts at not needing anything, and with this card reversed the expertise becomes a problem. You sleep badly and tell no one. You're stretched and you take on more. The worry is managed so well that it never gets felt, and the pressure builds up somewhere else, usually in the body or in a bleak mood that settles in over the weekend.

Family leans on you and you let it, and at work you can't delegate. A partner might say you've gone cold. Mars exalted keeps you going long past the point where you should stop, and Capricorn tends to wait for a crisis before asking. Ask someone for help with one practical thing you'd normally do yourself, and let them do it their way.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising meets the world composed, capable, a little formal, someone you'd trust with the keys. Saturn, ruler of your rising sign, gives you that grown-up air, probably even when you were twelve. With the Nine in the mask position, the composure is intact and you're running it on very little sleep, and the people who know you well can see strain at the edges.

Mars is exalted in Capricorn, so your instinctive response to a problem is disciplined action, and that serves you. The trouble is that the card's Mars is in Gemini, a quincunx from your rising sign, scattered and nervy, and your earth and the card's air pull opposite ways. So you're presenting a very solid front while your head goes in six directions. People will read you as in control. Strangers might find you a bit brusque, because holding it together takes the energy that usually goes into warmth.

In a leadership role, or anywhere you're expected to be the steady one, the pressure is sharpest. In an interview you'll come across well and then replay it all night. With family you might be the one making the arrangements while quietly frightened. Tell one colleague or friend that you're finding it a lot, in plain words, before it becomes obvious.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, Capricorn rising can freeze into formality. You get more reserved, more correct, harder to reach, and the worry hides behind good manners and a full calendar. Or the discipline cracks in some small public way, a snap at a junior colleague, a missed deadline, and you're more upset by it than anyone else is. Saturn, your chart ruler, likes to carry things alone.

Anything to do with authority or being judged brings it out. It can show in your posture, stiff and braced. The Three of Pentacles link says your sign works best alongside others, so find one person to share the load on the project that's worrying you, and let them see the unfinished bits.

sun.upright:
Gemini and Aquarius are both air signs, a trine apart, so this card speaks your language. That's a mixed blessing for an Aquarius Sun. You're here to think independently, see the bigger system, stand for something, and a shared element amplifies all of it. Your mind is your best tool, and the Nine of Swords is that tool running without supervision in the small hours.

Mars has no special dignity in Aquarius and picks up Saturn's colouring there, cool, strict, a bit severe. So your worry tends to be principled. It's the worry that you've been a hypocrite, that you've let down a cause or a group, that the world is heading somewhere bad and you're not doing enough about it. It's rarely about how you feel. You'll think about feelings, analyse them, and never quite feel them, which is part of why they come back at night. You can be quite alone with this, since you're the friend everyone comes to and seldom the one who asks.

Groups and friendships are the usual territory, the falling-out in the group chat, the committee, the community you've given years to. At work it's often an ethical question. The news may keep you up. Choose one worry you can actually do something about, however small, and do that one thing, and leave the rest to the rest of the world for a night.
sun.reversed:
Detachment is the Aquarius way of coping, and with this card reversed it gets turned right up. You step back so far from your own worry that you describe it like someone else's, interesting, a bit sad, nothing to do with you. It keeps you functional. It also keeps you lonely, and the worry is still there, running. Saturn's colouring on Mars in your sign makes you hard on yourself for struggling at all.

With friends you're always helping with their problems and never raising yours, and with causes you might throw yourself into something big so you don't have to feel something small. Sleep may be irregular. Tell a friend one feeling, using an actual feeling word, sad, scared, cross, and resist explaining it.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs air, room to think, friends who don't cling, and the sense that you can step back and look at your feelings from a little distance. Usually that works. The Nine drawn for your tides is when the stepping back turns into lying awake examining every emotion as though it were a problem to be solved.

The card and your Moon are both air, a trine apart, so they get on, and the element doubles. That means lots of thinking and not much feeling, which sounds calmer than it is. Mars in Aquarius borrows Saturn's tone, so the inner voice can be cold and judgemental. You may feel strangely numb and restless at the same time. Aquarius Moons often feel a bit different from the people around them, and at night that can become a fear that nobody really gets you, or that you don't really connect with anyone.

Friendships are central, a friend who's gone distant, a group you're drifting away from. The news and the wider world can press on you harder than you let on. Sleep tends to go when your routine goes. Instead of thinking about how you feel, write down three physical things you notice in your body when you wake, heart, stomach, shoulders, and leave it at that.
moon.reversed:
An Aquarius Moon can go very cool indeed when this card turns over. You stop reaching out. You're fine, you've got a lot on, and you drift from people without quite meaning to. The worry sits under a thick layer of reasonableness, and you can argue anyone, including yourself, out of noticing it. With your Moon sharing the card's element, the head wins every argument.

The friendships that need a bit of warmth to keep going are the first to suffer, and your hours get odd, up late at the computer, sleeping in on weekdays. Some of the people who love you may think you've gone off them. Saturn-coloured Mars is hard on you in private. Ring a friend instead of messaging, and ask about their week before you mention yours.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising comes across as friendly and a bit detached, interesting, hard to pin down, someone who doesn't quite fit the mould and doesn't want to. Saturn is your traditional chart ruler, Uranus the modern one. Drawn for your mask, the Nine adds a jittery quality to the calm, a mind visibly somewhere else, a faraway look that people read as coolness.

The card's sign and your rising sign are both air, a trine apart, which makes it easy for Mars in Gemini to come straight through your manner. You're quick, clever, a bit sharp, and you may argue a point you don't even care about. Mars in Aquarius has no dignity and picks up Saturn's colouring, so the edge is cool. People can find you intimidating or remote without you meaning it at all. The tension is that Aquarius rising likes to seem unbothered, and this card is very bothered indeed.

In groups it shows most, at work, in a club, in a friend group, where you might play the outsider harder than usual. Online you can be sharper than you'd ever be face to face. First meetings may feel oddly formal. At the next group thing, pick one person, ask them something personal and kind, and stay with their answer.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising with the Nine reversed turns detachment into a wall. People meet a cool, clever person who seems not to need anyone, and they leave you alone, which is exactly what the worry wanted. Or you swing into contrariness, disagreeing with the room for the sake of it, defending an opinion you don't even hold just to keep people at arm's length.

Groups and online spaces are where it's most obvious, along with a social exhaustion where every event feels like too much. Colleagues may find you hard to read. Saturn as chart ruler can make you stern with others when the real sternness is aimed at yourself. Say yes to one invitation from someone warm, and stay long enough to have a proper conversation.

sun.upright:
Look at the quilt in this card, covered in roses and little astrological symbols. That's the part a Pisces Sun tends to miss when this card turns up. You're here to feel, imagine, care for people and soften the edges between yourself and everything else, and when you worry, your imagination does the worrying, so it's vivid, detailed and very convincing.

Gemini squares Pisces. They're both mutable signs and the friction between them forces something to shift. Mars has no special dignity in Pisces and takes on Jupiter's colouring there, and Neptune's in the modern reading, so it spreads and blurs. Thoughts and feelings flood each other with no clear line between them, since air and water have never been properly introduced. Pisces also absorbs other people's worry, so some of what's keeping you up may not even be yours. Mars rules the last ten degrees of Pisces through the Ten of Cups, the happy family under the rainbow, which is the dream your sign is working toward. This card is often the fear of losing it.

A friend in trouble is common ground for it, someone you've taken on and can't stop thinking about. Creative work can stall, because the imagination is busy elsewhere. Sleep and dreams will be vivid. Before bed, ask yourself of each worry whether it's yours or someone else's, and put down the ones that aren't yours, even just by saying the person's name and 'not mine' out loud.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with the Nine upside down often escapes. Sleep too much, drink a bit more, disappear into a book or a series or someone else's crisis, anywhere the worry can't follow. It's gentle and it's understandable. The worry follows anyway, only more slowly. Pisces is a mutable water sign and takes the shape of whatever holds it, avoidance included.

Deadlines slip, messages go unanswered, money leaks out on small comforts. In a relationship you can be so tuned in to the other person that your own fear never gets aired. Jupiter's colouring on Mars makes all of it spread. Choose one worry and give it a practical shape, a phone call, a form, an appointment, and do it before lunch.

moon.upright:
Pisces Moon feelings have no walls. You pick up the mood of the room, the news, the friend who rang crying, and you carry it home and into bed. This card in your tides tends to arrive in dreams as much as in waking, vivid ones, strange ones, and you may wake not quite sure where the dream stopped.

Mars has no dignity in Pisces and takes on Jupiter's expansiveness, so feelings spread and grow. Gemini and Pisces square each other, and that friction shows as a restless mind grinding against a Moon that wants to float. The card's element and yours are neutral to each other, and at night nobody makes the introduction. So the thoughts churn and the feelings flood, and you can't tell which started it. There's often guilt in this for Pisces, a sense of having not helped enough or been kind enough, and it tends to be well out of proportion.

Sleep is the main event. Alcohol or late screens can make the dreams worse, and you'll know which. With a friend or family member in difficulty you may be absorbing far too much. Keep your evenings quieter than usual, no news after dinner, and put something with a calming smell by the bed, lavender or clean washing, something that tells your body it's time to stop.
moon.reversed:
Sleep itself is where the fear goes for a Pisces Moon when this card is reversed. You sleep a lot, or at odd hours, and wake unrested. Daydreaming takes up more of the day. It feels like tiredness and partly it is, and partly it's a way of floating above something you don't want to land on. Mars in your Moon's sign takes on Jupiter's appetite, so an escape that starts small can grow quite quietly.

Friends drift, creative work gets abandoned halfway, and you may lean on one person until they're your whole support. The Ten of Cups link says your Moon longs for a settled, happy home, so check whether the worry is really about that. Talk to one person about it over tea, in the afternoon, in plain terms.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising comes across soft, open, a little dreamy, and people tell you things. Jupiter rules your rising sign traditionally, Neptune in modern charts, and both give you that permeable quality, as if you'd taken in the whole room before you've said hello. When this card is your mask, what you're taking in is worry, and some of it shows.

The square between Gemini and Pisces makes for friction, and Mars in Pisces takes on Jupiter's colouring, which spreads things out. So a nervous thought doesn't stay small. You walk into the meeting and pick up that someone's tense, and by lunch you've decided it's about you. Air and water don't naturally speak to each other, and people may read you as vague or distracted when really you're overwhelmed by input. The tiredness shows in your face before it shows anywhere else.

Crowds are where it's strongest, the office, the train, a party. At work you might be everyone's confidant and exhausted by it. With a partner you may be reading moods that aren't there. Before a busy day, give yourself ten minutes alone somewhere quiet, a walk, a bath, the car with the engine off, and decide which one thing you'll leave at the door.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising tends to vanish when the Nine is reversed. You go vague, drift out of conversations, stop answering the door, and people assume you're just being dreamy. Or you take on everyone's problems in a sort of rescue mode so nobody notices that you're the one who needs rescuing. The square from Gemini means the worry never settles, it just changes shape.

At work it's the colleague you're propping up, and socially it's the plans you keep half-making. Your face often gives it away before you do. Jupiter as chart ruler makes the giving bigger than it needs to be. Say no to one person who leans on you, gently, and use the time for something that's only for you.

1.upright:
Your body tends to get the news first when this card lands in the first house. This is you as you walk out the door, your face, your health, your energy, the way you start things. Mars is the house's natural ruler, so the card is on home ground, and Mercury, Gemini's ruler, has its joy here too. That's a lot of fast, sharp energy on the most visible corner of the chart. The first house is angular, and what's in it gets seen.

What you'll feel is a nervy alertness. Sleep gets shorter. You wake sharp and already thinking, and the thinking shows in your face and posture. Gemini sits a sextile from Aries, the first house's natural sign, and air feeds fire, so the worry spreads quickly and turns physical, a tight jaw, restless legs, a readiness to argue. This is also the house of beginnings, and with the Nine here you may be second-guessing a fresh start, whether you're up to it, whether it was a mistake to begin at all.

How you're sleeping, what you're eating, whether you've moved, those are the first places to look. Appearance too, and you might stop caring or care far too much. A new start, a job, a city, a new look, may be where the doubt lives. Put your body first for a while, early nights, a daily walk, plenty of water, and let the big questions about who you are wait until you've slept.
1.reversed:
In the first house the reversed Nine often looks like pushing through. You feel ragged and you go harder, more exercise, more coffee, more bravado, so nobody sees you flagging. Mars on home turf doesn't like being seen to retreat. The worry goes into the body instead and shows as tension, clumsiness, a short fuse. Or you retreat from being seen at all, and hide the face that's showing the strain.

It turns up in how you start the day, rushed and on edge, and in a new venture you keep putting off or charging at without thinking. People may find you a bit combative. Build one slow minute into each morning before the phone comes on, and notice what your body is telling you.

2.upright:
Money worry is the plainest reading of this card in the second house, and usually the right one. This is money you can actually count, what you own, what you earn, and the less obvious part, what you think you're worth. Bills, rent, savings running down, whether you're charging enough. Taurus is this house's natural sign, and Taurus is where Mars sits in detriment, so the card's way of working runs against what the house wants. The house wants to hold still and build. The card wants to think about it all night.

Air and earth make poor partners, so there's friction between the idea of the money and the money itself. You worry in general terms, it's all going wrong, I'll never get ahead, and the worry never touches the actual figures. The second house is succedent, where you build up and hold, and it's slow by nature. The Nine is quick and loud, and it can make you panic about something that needs a steady hand. Self-worth is tangled up in it too. When money's tight it's very easy to decide you're not worth much either.

Your bank account and your pay are the obvious places, a raise you haven't asked for, an invoice you haven't chased. Spending to soothe is another, the late-night online order. Get the real numbers out on paper one morning, what's coming in and what's going out, all on one page, and let that page be what you look at when the worry starts.
2.reversed:
The reversed Nine in the second house often means not looking. Statements go unopened, the banking app stays shut, and the worry runs under everything as a low hum. Mars in detriment in Taurus can't fight its way out, so it avoids. Sometimes it's the reverse, checking the balance ten times a day and still feeling poor no matter what it says.

Underneath there's often a lingering sense that you don't deserve more, which keeps you undercharging or not asking. Earth and air disagree here, and the idea of the money has come loose from the money. There are small leaks too, subscriptions you forgot, spending you don't remember. Pick a set time each week to look at your money, same day, same hour, and keep the appointment even when the numbers aren't nice.

3.upright:
This is a Gemini card in Gemini's own house. The third is the natural home of words, messages, brothers and sisters, neighbours, short trips and learning, and the Nine belongs here. The element matches too, air on air, so the card plays at full volume in the third house, for better and for too much. The Moon has its joy in this house, which is worth knowing, because feelings and everyday talk get mixed up very easily here.

What you'll recognise is the mind that won't stop talking. You draft messages you never send. You replay a conversation with your brother or your neighbour and find a new insult in it each time. Mars as a guest in Gemini fights with words, and in the house of words it has plenty to work with. The third house is cadent, the part of the chart that processes and adjusts, and that's the upside. This is thinking that can turn into learning, once it's out of your head and on paper or said aloud.

Messages are the main place, the group chat, the text left on read, the email you're dreading. A sibling or cousin may be part of it. The daily commute can be where the loop starts. Write the message you're afraid to send, in full, then wait a day before deciding whether to send it, and if you do, cut it by half first.
3.reversed:
Words stop flowing, or they flood. With the Nine reversed in the third house you might avoid the call, leave the message on read, go quiet with a sibling for weeks. Or you say too much, the sharp reply, the long rant, the thing you can't take back. Gemini territory is all about exchange, and here the exchange has either stalled or boiled over.

Family group chats and neighbours feel it, and so does study, a course that stalls because you can't concentrate. It can look like reading everything and taking none of it in. Sleep is often busy with talk. Choose the one conversation you've been dodging and have it in person or by phone, and keep it short.

4.upright:
Worry that lives at home is the hardest kind to get away from, and that's what this card brings to the fourth house. This is the actual house or flat, the family you came from, and the private ground you go back to at the end of the day. It sits at the bottom of the chart and it's angular, so what happens here matters a great deal even when nobody outside sees it. It's in the bedroom at night, and very often it's about family.

Cancer is this house's natural sign, and Cancer is the sign of Mars's fall, where it's uncomfortable and can't act directly. So conflict in this house tends to go round the long way. Nobody has the argument. Everyone lies awake. Gemini and Cancer are neighbours with little in common, and the card's air and the house's water have to be introduced before they'll work together, so thinking about home and feeling about home don't quite connect. You may know exactly what's wrong and still not be able to say it at the dinner table.

A parent is often at the centre of it, their health, their money, the old dynamic. The house itself can be the worry, a lease, repairs, a move. Old family memories may come up. Make the bedroom a place for sleep only for a while, no laptop, no bills on the bedside table, and have one honest conversation with the family member it concerns.
4.reversed:
Home gets very tidy when this card is reversed in the fourth house. You clean, you fix, you keep everyone fed, and nobody talks about the thing. Mars in fall can't push its way to the surface, so it stays in the walls of the place. Sometimes it's avoiding home altogether, working late, staying out, finding reasons to be anywhere else.
