Look at the phone call to a parent you keep putting off, the room nobody uses, the repair you keep not arranging. Sleep may be poor because the bedroom doesn't feel restful any more. Pick one physical thing in the home to sort out, the drawer, the leak, the lock, and let doing it be a way in to the conversation.

5.upright:
Something you love is keeping you up. The fifth house is where you play, romance, creativity, children, hobbies, the things you do for the joy of it, and Venus has her joy here. So the Nine in this house is worry turning up where there's meant to be delight. You've made something and can't stop picking at it. You're falling for someone and lying awake over their last message. You love your kids and the love has gone anxious.

Gemini is a sextile from Leo, the fifth's natural sign, and the card's air gets the house's fire going, so the worry catches easily and burns hot. The fifth is also about being seen to shine, and the fear underneath is usually of looking foolish. Mars has no particular dignity in Leo and borrows the Sun's pride, so you might feel defensive about whatever you love most. It stops being fun because it matters so much.

In a new romance it's the overthinking, the checking, the wondering. With children it can be worry about their school, their friends, their future. With a creative project it's the paralysis just before you share it. Do one playful thing where there's nothing at stake, a board game, a doodle, a dance class, and do it badly on purpose.
5.reversed:
In the fifth house the reversed Nine tends to kill the fun quietly. You stop doing the hobby, stop dating, put the creative project in a drawer, and tell yourself you're too busy. The real reason is that it's become frightening. Mars borrows Leo's pride here and would sooner give something up than be seen doing it badly. Or you throw yourself at pleasure to drown out the worry, big nights, reckless crushes, spending on treats.

Romance goes flat, creative work blocks, and with kids anxiety can turn into hovering. Your partner or a child may notice you've gone serious. Take the project out of the drawer and show it to one friend, and ask only what they enjoyed about it.

6.upright:
Mars has its joy in the sixth house, the house of daily work, routine and the body's upkeep. That's the most useful fact about this pairing. The planet behind the Nine of Swords does its best work here, when it has tasks, a list, a body to look after. What's keeping you up in this house is usually the ordinary grind, the workload, the colleague, the body's small complaints. It's also where the energy that's keeping you up belongs.

Gemini squares Virgo, this house's natural sign, both mutable, so there's friction that forces something in the routine to change. Air and earth pull against each other, and you'll feel it as a gap between what you know you should do, sleep, eat properly, move, and what you actually do. The sixth house is cadent, it processes and adjusts, and it's slow and practical by nature. The Nine makes it jittery. You lie awake doing the next day's tasks in your head, and then you're too tired to do them.

Sleep is the obvious thing to look at, and your working day is the other. A colleague or a boss may be part of the worry, or it may be sheer volume. Look after the body's upkeep, walks, meals at regular times, less caffeine after lunch. Take the list that runs through your head at night and do the worst item on it first thing, while you still have energy.
6.reversed:
Running yourself into the ground is the usual shape of this card reversed in the sixth house. Mars in its joy here likes to work, and when it's blocked it overworks, extra hours, skipped lunches, a routine so packed there's no room to feel anything. Or the routine falls apart altogether and you're sleeping at odd times, eating at the desk, never quite on top of things.

You'll know it by how tired you are, by small niggles that won't clear up, and by resentment at work. If your sleep has been poor for weeks, it's worth mentioning to your GP. Otherwise, choose one habit to protect, the same bedtime, a lunch away from the screen, and keep it for a month.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite you, a partner, a spouse, a business partner, sometimes an open rival, anyone you deal with one to one. Libra is its natural sign, and Mars in Libra is in detriment, so the card's way of doing things runs against what this house wants. The house wants fairness and balance. The card wants to fight about it in your head in the dark. The seventh is angular, so whatever's happening here is out in the open, or about to be.

The card and this house share an element and sit a trine apart, air to air, which means there's a lot of talk. You go over what they said and what you said and what you meant. Every conversation gets a second and third hearing after the lights are off. Mars being weak in Libra means the fight rarely happens face to face. You smooth it over in person and then have it alone, and often you're arguing with a version of them that isn't quite the real one.

A partner is the main place, a disagreement, a doubt, a feeling of not being heard. A contract or agreement may also be on your mind, the terms, whether you signed the right thing. A rival at work can take up far too much room. Have the conversation you keep having in your head, with the actual person, and let them tell you their side.
7.reversed:
Unspoken worry about a partner can sit for so long in the seventh house that it turns into distance. You're polite, you're kind, and you're not really there. Mars in detriment in Libra can't bring itself to start the fight, so the fear lies between you in the bed. You can end up keeping score silently while telling everyone things are fine.

Or it comes out all at once, an argument that seems to come from nowhere, about something small. Business deals can go quiet the same way, and so can things with anyone you've been avoiding. Air on air keeps the private commentary fluent, so it never feels urgent to say any of it. Say one honest, unpolished thing to your partner, without rehearsing it first, and give them time to answer.

8.upright:
Shared money, debt, inheritance, sex and intimacy, the things that end and the fear of losing what you love. That's the eighth house, the deep end of the chart. Mars is its natural ruler in the old tradition, so this card is on home turf here and strong. That doesn't make it easy. It means the worry has real force, and it goes straight for what's most private.

Gemini and Scorpio, the house's natural sign, are a quincunx apart, nothing in common, constant small adjustment. The card wants to talk it through, and the house wants to go silent and deep. Air and water are strangers, and in this house they rarely get introduced. So your mind may be racing around something you can barely say out loud, a fear about a partner's loyalty, money you owe, a loss you haven't grieved. The eighth house is succedent and holds on, which is why the same fear can come back night after night.

Shared money is a common place for it, a joint account, a debt, a will or an inheritance. Intimacy is another, fear of being close or fear of losing someone close. An ending may be in the background, a relationship, a job, a stage of life. Pick the one thing you've never said about it, and say it to someone you trust, somewhere private, with time to talk.
8.reversed:
Secrets keep well in the eighth house, and with the Nine reversed the fear often gets locked in a box and the box gets buried. You don't talk about the debt, the grief, the thing in the relationship. Mars on home turf is capable of keeping a secret for years. It leaks out as control, jealousy, a need to know where everyone is and what they're spending.

Or you go the other way and pick at it constantly, going over the loss or the betrayal until it's all you think about. Shared finances, closeness that's gone guarded, and endings you haven't let finish all carry it. Open one of the boxes, the statement, the old letter, the conversation, with someone beside you who can hold their nerve.

9.upright:
Across the zodiac from Gemini sits Sagittarius, the ninth house's natural sign, so this card faces the house head on. The ninth is the long view, study, travel, belief, law, publishing, anything that takes you further than your usual streets. Gemini wants detail and the ninth wants meaning. When the Nine lands here the detail wins and the meaning goes missing, and you lie awake over the small print of a big decision.

The Sun has its joy in the ninth, and it's normally a bright, hopeful house. Air and fire feed each other, so ideas catch quickly, and the Nine turns that speed against you. A doubt about your beliefs, or about a course you've started, spreads until it feels like the whole direction of your life is wrong. The opposition is a pull toward balance, somewhere between Gemini's facts and Sagittarius's faith, and you'll probably need a bit of both.

Study and exams are common ground, an essay, a qualification, a thesis. Travel, visas, a move abroad or a long trip may be on your mind. A legal matter can also sit in this house. Write down the big question you're worrying about, list the three facts you'd need to answer it, and go and find the first one.
9.reversed:
Faith tends to go quietly when the Nine is reversed in the ninth house. You stop studying, stop planning the trip, stop believing in the thing you used to talk about with such conviction. Or you go the other way and cling to a belief harder than ever to keep the doubt at bay, arguing about it with anyone who'll listen. Mars borrows Jupiter's size in Sagittarius, so the doubt can feel like it's about everything.

Courses get dropped, travel plans get shelved, and debates online leave you shaking. A teacher or mentor might be part of the picture. Go back to one source you used to trust, a book, a teacher, a place, and see how it looks to you with fresh eyes.

10.upright:
Mars is exalted in Capricorn, the tenth house's natural sign, so the card's planet is welcomed at the top of the chart. The tenth is your career, your reputation, what you're known for, the boss and the public. That welcome is worth holding on to. The drive behind the Nine of Swords, pointed outward, is exactly what this house rewards. The trouble is that it's pointing at you.

Gemini and Capricorn are a quincunx apart, and the card's air and the house's earth disagree, talk against proof. The tenth wants results you can show. The card offers a mind racing over how you're seen, whether you're good enough, whether they've noticed the mistake. It's an angular house, very visible, and that visibility is part of the pressure. You're worried about being judged, and in this house you are being judged, which makes the worry feel justified even when it's well out of proportion.

Work is the whole territory, a performance review, a promotion, a manager whose silence you keep reading into. Your public reputation can be involved, what people say, what's online. A parent's expectations sometimes sit in the tenth too. Take the fear about your work to someone senior you trust, and ask them straight how you're doing.
10.reversed:
In the tenth house the reversed Nine often shows as grinding on. You keep working, keep delivering, keep smiling at the boss, and the fear goes unspoken. Mars exalted here is very good at effort, which means the worry can be hidden for a long time under results. Or ambition freezes, and you stop putting yourself forward because you're sure you'll be found out.

Burnout creeps in, a career move keeps not being made, and there's an odd defensiveness whenever anyone gives you feedback. The quincunx with Gemini means your head and your job are hard to line up. Ask for one piece of honest feedback from someone whose opinion counts, and write down what they say, word for word.

11.upright:
The eleventh house is friends, networks, the groups you belong to, and your hopes for the future. Aquarius is its natural sign, and Gemini is a trine from Aquarius, both air, so the card sits easily here and the element doubles. Jupiter has its joy in this house, which usually makes it generous and hopeful. With the Nine in it, the generosity goes anxious.

What you'll recognise is social worry. You replay the party, what you said, who didn't laugh. You wonder whether the group has moved on without you. The doubled element makes the thinking quick, articulate and very persuasive at two in the morning. The eleventh is a succedent house, it builds and holds, and it holds on to slights as much as anything. Hopes for the future can turn into dread about it as well, a plan for the next few years that suddenly looks foolish.

Friendships are the main territory, a friend who's gone quiet, a falling-out in the group. Online communities and group chats come into it. A club, a team or a committee may be part of it. Message the friend you're worried about, keep it light and warm, and let their reply be the evidence instead of your theory.
11.reversed:
Pulling back from people is how the reversed Nine often shows in the eleventh house. You skip the group thing, mute the chat, let friendships lapse because it's easier than worrying about them. Or you over-invest in one friend or one group and feel crushed by small slights. Hopes for the future can shrink to getting through the week.

Friendships go cold and you feel on the outside of every circle, and there are hopes you've stopped letting yourself have. Jupiter's joy here usually brings people toward you, and when you stop showing up, that flow stops too. The trine with Aquarius makes the thinking fluent, and fluent thinking can talk you out of any invitation. Say yes to one group thing, and stay until you've had one real conversation.

12.upright:
A bed in a dark room is most of what's on this card, and the twelfth house is the house of sleep, dreams, retreat, and what's hidden, the things you don't show and sometimes don't know about yourself. So the card has arrived somewhere it recognises. Pisces sits on this house by nature, and Gemini squares Pisces, both mutable, which makes friction that forces something to shift. Saturn has its joy in the twelfth. This is the house where solitude can do you good, and the Nine makes it lonely.

What you'll feel is the unconscious getting loud. Dreams are vivid, you wake with a feeling you can't place, and fears you thought were dealt with come back in the dark. The card's air and the house's water are neutral to each other and need someone to introduce them, so the thoughts and the feelings don't match. You might be anxious about nothing you can name. The twelfth is cadent, a house of letting go, and what the card is pushing up is usually something that's ready to be let go of.

Sleep is the whole of it for many people, the quality, the dreams, the hour you wake. Old guilt or a secret may be surfacing. Time alone matters, and you may need more of it, the right kind. Give yourself a proper wind-down, the same hour, the same routine, and if a dream stays with you in the morning, tell someone about it over breakfast.
12.reversed:
Reversed in the twelfth house, the Nine often goes further underground. You don't dream, or you don't remember the dreams. You feel fine and tired at once. The worry is still there, just below the surface, and it shows up in odd ways, a sudden tearfulness, a bad mood with no cause, a pull to hide away for days. The square from Gemini keeps the mind busy enough that you never quite feel it.

Sleep gets long and unrefreshing, retreat turns into isolation, and there may be secrets you're carrying for yourself or for someone else. Saturn in its joy here can make solitude useful, so take some time alone on purpose, a quiet walk, an hour in a church or a garden, and let whatever comes up come up.
